notes.author: human:project-owner
notes.text: One Switch instance must operate several projects concurrently; switching one project must not stop the others.

problem: Developers manually stop and restart development servers when moving between Git worktrees, and the workflow becomes error-prone when several related repositories run at the same time.

risk.rollback: Disable process mutation and retain read-only worktree discovery if lifecycle management cannot reliably isolate projects and terminate complete child process trees.

scope: Create a local control plane that registers multiple Git repositories, discovers their worktrees, and maintains one independently switchable server slot with a stable port for each project.
Include serialized lifecycle operations per project, readiness checks, isolated logs, loopback-only control endpoints, and reconciliation after control-plane restart.
title: Run and switch multiple worktree-backed projects
validation: Run at least three fixture projects concurrently, switch each to another worktree, and verify that only the selected project's process restarts while every project keeps its configured port.
Verify concurrent requests for one project are serialized, failures are isolated, stale paths and arbitrary commands are rejected, and the dashboard reports readiness and logs accurately.
value: A developer can move an entire local stack between branches from one dashboard without repeatedly navigating directories or disturbing unrelated services.
